about: M. Chapoutier has been based in Tain-l’Hermitage, at the foot of the famous Hermitage hill, since 1808. Michel Chapoutier, who leads the house today, made it one of the early champions of biodynamic farming in France, practiced since 1991. Crozes-Hermitage is the larger appellation that surrounds the Hermitage hill, and Sicamor is Chapoutier’s Crozes red, a step up from its classic bottling, assembled to show the appellation’s different soils in one wine.

Sicamor is 100% Syrah, farmed organically and biodynamically and picked by hand. It blends three terroirs: coarse Tournon granite to the west of the Hermitage hill, puddingstone to the east, and a terrace of river alluvium at Les Chassis. The grapes are destemmed and fermented for about ten days in rough concrete, with a maceration of four to five weeks. The wine then goes into barrel warm and ages about 12 months in seasoned demi-muids, followed by around six months in concrete.
